title: DynamicInfer: Runtime-Aware Sparse Offloading for LLMs Inference on a Consumer-Grade GPU
claim: Existing offloading schemes either move whole weights or split work statically across devices; ours (sparsity-aware hybrid) computes only active neurons where they reside.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, GPU over CPU stacks, numbered circle steps, shared legend
description: Three side-by-side panels compare offloading strategies: GPU-Centric Offloading, GPU-CPU Hybrid Offloading, and PowerInfer's Sparsity-Aware Hybrid Offloading. Each panel stacks a GPU box above a CPU box, joined by a thick black bar. Each box is split by a dashed line into Memory on the left and Core on the right. Gray weight blocks hold small red (activated) and yellow (inactive) neuron squares. Dotted light-blue squares are cores. Numbered circles (1, 2, 3) mark the order of steps. Black arrows show transfers and blue arrows show computation. Result boxes labeled CPU Results and GPU Results show where outputs are merged. A legend at the bottom explains the colors and arrows. The eye goes first to the three bold titles, then to the red neuron blocks. The caption is only 'Offloading System'. The figure appears to be a background-motivation figure, and it shows PowerInfer as the latest prior approach rather than the paper's own method.
caption: Offloading System
abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in various NLP tasks, but their enormous memory footprints pose significant challenges for deployment on consumer-grade GPUs. Prior solutions, such as PowerInfer, combine offloading and sparse activation to reduce memory and computational overhead, but suffer from static neuron partitioning, leading to suboptimal GPU utilization and increased latency. In this work, we present DynamicInfer, a runtime neuron offloading framework that dynamically adapts neuron scheduling based on input-dependent activation patterns. DynamicInfer introduces (1) a hierarchical neural caching strategies, (2) a load-aware neuron activation mechanism tailored to heterogeneous hardware, and (3) an activation-aware prefetching pipeline that overlaps data transfer with computation. Extensive experiments on ReluLLaMA and Prosparse models across multiple hardware platforms demonstrate that DynamicInfer achieves up to 253\% speedup over llama.cpp and 59\% over PowerInfer, while retaining model accuracy. Our approach offers a practical and scalable solution for high-performance LLM inference on resource-constrained devices.
